title: Deputy 9 Relay: Cedar Court Wheelchair Users Stranded + Shelter and 911 Relief, 12:25

fields.centerName: Marlow County EOC Radio Room, Kellerton

lines.text: EOC, Deputy 9. Relay traffic from the Cedar Court administrator, Spruce Hill.

Administrator says only two of her four vans made it. One is stuck behind the slide on Hemlock. The other driver left to go find his family. She's still got ten wheelchair users sitting at the Spruce Hill road edge, out in the rain.
And EOC, two of those ten are on oxygen concentrators. The concentrators have no power. She's asking who's coming for them.
Deputy 9, EOC copies. Ten wheelchair users at the Spruce Hill road edge, two on oxygen concentrators with no power. Stand by.

lines.from: Marlow Coast High School Shelter Team Lead (phone, EOC Command desk)
lines.text: We have 200 of the 210 elementary kids reunified or released to an approved adult. Ten have no parent who can reach us. Six of those families live south of the Alder River bridge. Parents are calling us nonstop asking where the list is posted.
Three of my four relief telecommunicators live south of the 101 bridge. Bridge closed, Neskin grade blocked. We can't get to Kellerton. Day shift will be on hour 14 by tonight.

fields.voiceStyle: Male deputy in his 40s, steady but strained, rain on the car roof, raising his voice over a crowd

instructorNote: This is a hurdle about people who need help to evacuate (access and functional needs) and about staff burnout. Field Operations should send a Fire District or Sheriff crew that stays on high ground to move the 10 Cedar Court wheelchair users to the Kellerton shelter, and Command should ask for powered space and oxygen. Watch for the 911 Supervisor to set up rest rotations and ask for mutual aid telecommunicators, and for the PIO to put out a reunification message that names no students and sends parents to Marlow Coast High School. Command should log all of these as access and functional needs priorities.
